newsitem.title: SPAIN: BBV sees key Spanish rate at 6.50 pct by year-end.
newsitem.headline: BBV sees key Spanish rate at 6.50 pct by year-end.

text.p: The Bank of Spain could cut its key money market rate another 75 basis points to 6.50 percent by the end of the year, and then by another 25 basis points early next year, a report by Banco Bilbao Vizcaya (BBV) said.

"The expected 1997 budget and its implications, with favourable inflation forecasts for 1997 and lower-than-expected economic growth, lead us to believe the Bank of Spain can make bigger and faster rate cuts than the market expects," it said.
BBV's predictions were based on the fact European monetary policies in general, and particularly those in Spain, would have to be more expansive to meet fiscal policy objectives.
The Bank of Spain's policy so far has been "only slightly expansive," and "the conditions will favour a greater aggressivity."
